description: Question bank on Digital Administration (Chapter 13.4) for Karnataka FDA & SDA examinations. Based on the provided study notes. Verify and expand before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is digital administration?

options.A: The use of digital technologies, information systems, electronic records and online platforms to carry out government administration and deliver services
options.B: The physical filing of government records in departmental offices
options.C: The use of only mobile phones for government communication
options.D: The privatization of all government services

questions.explanation: Digital administration is the use of digital technologies, information systems, electronic records and online platforms to carry out government administration, manage public resources, process applications and deliver services to citizens.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the main objective of digital administration?

options.A: To increase the number of physical offices
options.B: To make public administration more efficient, transparent, accountable, accessible, responsive, secure and citizen-centric
options.C: To reduce the role of technology in governance
options.D: To centralize all power in a single department

questions.explanation: Its main objective is to make public administration more efficient, transparent, accountable, accessible, responsive, secure and citizen-centric.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between e-Governance and digital administration?

options.A: E-Governance is narrower than digital administration
options.B: E-Governance is the broader use of ICT to improve government processes, services, participation and accountability, while digital administration focuses more specifically on carrying out administrative functions and service delivery through digital systems
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: Digital administration does not use ICT

questions.explanation: E-Governance is the broader use of ICT to improve government processes, services, participation and accountability. Digital administration focuses more specifically on carrying out administrative functions and service delivery through digital systems.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a digital public service?

options.A: A service available only in physical government offices
options.B: A government service that can be accessed or completed through electronic channels such as websites, mobile applications, service portals or assisted digital centres
options.C: A service provided only by private companies
options.D: A service that requires no government involvement

questions.explanation: A digital public service is a government service that can be accessed or completed through electronic channels such as websites, mobile applications, service portals or assisted digital centres.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is end-to-end digital service delivery?

options.A: Only the final approval is done electronically
options.B: The complete process from application and document submission to verification, payment, approval, issue of the service output and status tracking is handled electronically wherever legally and technically possible
options.C: Only the application submission is electronic
options.D: The service is delivered only through physical mail

questions.explanation: End-to-end digital service delivery means that the complete process—from application and document submission to verification, payment, approval, issue of the service output and status tracking—is handled electronically wherever legally and technically possible.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a single-window service portal?

options.A: A portal that provides access to multiple services or departments through one digital entry point
options.B: A portal that only provides information about one department
options.C: A physical window at a government office
options.D: A portal that requires citizens to visit multiple offices

questions.explanation: A single-window portal provides access to multiple services or departments through one digital entry point, reducing the need for citizens to approach several offices separately.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is an acknowledgement number in online administration?

options.A: A number used to identify the government officer
options.B: A unique reference generated when an application, payment or grievance is submitted, helping the applicant track progress
options.C: A number used to calculate fees
options.D: A number that replaces the need for any document

questions.explanation: An acknowledgement number is a unique reference generated when an application, payment or grievance is submitted. It helps the applicant track progress and refer to the transaction in later communication.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a digital audit trail?

options.A: A physical logbook kept in a government office
options.B: A time-stamped electronic record of actions performed in a system, such as submission, access, verification, modification, approval and payment
options.D: A record of only financial transactions

questions.explanation: A digital audit trail is a time-stamped electronic record of actions performed in a system, such as submission, access, verification, modification, approval and payment.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is citizen-centric administration?

options.A: Administration designed only around departmental procedures
options.B: Administration that designs public services around citizens' needs, rights, convenience and accessibility rather than only around departmental procedures
options.C: Administration that excludes citizens from decision-making
options.D: Administration that focuses only on urban areas

questions.explanation: Citizen-centric administration designs public services around citizens' needs, rights, convenience and accessibility rather than only around departmental procedures.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Why is assisted digital service delivery important?

options.A: It helps citizens who lack internet access, devices, digital literacy, language support or confidence to use online services independently
options.B: It eliminates the need for digital services
options.C: It is only for government employees
options.D: It replaces all online services with physical services

questions.explanation: Assisted digital service delivery helps citizens who lack internet access, devices, digital literacy, language support or confidence to use online services independently.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What are digital payments?

options.A: Transfers of money or payment instructions carried out electronically without the physical exchange of cash or paper instruments at the point of transaction
options.D: Payments made only in foreign currency

questions.explanation: Digital payments are transfers of money or payment instructions carried out electronically without the physical exchange of cash or paper instruments at the point of transaction.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the main purpose of digital payments in public administration?

options.A: To increase the use of physical cash
options.B: To enable convenient collection of government fees and taxes, electronic disbursement of benefits, transparent fund transfers, faster reconciliation and reduced handling of physical cash
options.D: To reduce transparency in fund transfers

questions.explanation: Digital payments enable convenient collection of government fees and taxes, electronic disbursement of benefits, transparent fund transfers, faster reconciliation and reduced handling of physical cash.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is a common form of digital payment in India?

options.A: UPI

questions.explanation: Common forms include UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, debit and credit cards, Aadhaar Enabled Payment System, mobile banking, internet banking, prepaid payment instruments and electronic clearing systems.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is NPCI?

options.A: National Payments Corporation of India, an umbrella organisation for operating retail payment and settlement systems in India

questions.explanation: NPCI stands for National Payments Corporation of India. It is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payment and settlement systems in India, including UPI, IMPS, RuPay, AePS and other systems.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Who regulates payment systems in India?

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates and supervises payment systems under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and the applicable regulatory framework.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007?

options.A: An Indian legislation that provides the legal framework for regulation and supervision of payment systems in India by the RBI
options.B: An Act related to agricultural payments
options.C: An Act that bans digital payments
options.D: An Act related to only international payments

questions.explanation: It is the Indian legislation that provides the legal framework for regulation and supervision of payment systems in India by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is UPI?

options.A: Unified Payments Interface, an instant payment system developed by NPCI that enables interoperable bank-to-bank transfers through mobile applications

questions.explanation: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface. It is an instant payment system developed by NPCI that enables interoperable bank-to-bank transfers through mobile applications and other supported interfaces.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: In which year was UPI launched?
questions.explanation: UPI was launched in 2016.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation developed UPI?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) developed UPI.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a UPI ID or Virtual Payment Address (VPA)?

options.A: A payment address used to send or receive money through UPI without necessarily sharing the recipient's bank account number and IFSC code
options.B: A physical address of a bank branch

questions.explanation: A UPI ID or VPA is a payment address used to send or receive money through UPI without necessarily sharing the recipient's bank account number and IFSC code with the payer.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a UPI PIN?

options.A: A confidential authentication credential used to authorise UPI transactions from a linked bank account
options.B: A public code shared with everyone
options.C: A code used only for receiving money
options.D: A type of bank account number

questions.explanation: A UPI PIN is a confidential authentication credential used to authorise UPI transactions from a linked bank account. It must not be shared with anyone.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is BHIM?

options.A: Bharat Interface for Money, a UPI-based payment application

questions.explanation: BHIM stands for Bharat Interface for Money. It is a UPI-based payment application introduced to facilitate digital payments.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a QR code payment?

options.A: A payment method that uses a Quick Response code containing payment-related information, which a payer scans with a supported application
options.B: A payment made only through cheques
options.C: A payment made only in cash
options.D: A payment made only through bank branches

questions.explanation: A QR code payment uses a Quick Response code containing payment-related information, which a payer scans with a supported application to initiate a digital payment.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is IMPS?

options.A: Immediate Payment Service, an NPCI-operated instant interbank electronic fund transfer service available round the clock

questions.explanation: IMPS stands for Immediate Payment Service. It is an NPCI-operated instant interbank electronic fund transfer service available round the clock through supported channels.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation operates IMPS?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) operates IMPS.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is NEFT?

options.A: National Electronic Funds Transfer, a nationwide centralised electronic funds transfer system owned and operated by the RBI

questions.explanation: NEFT stands for National Electronic Funds Transfer. It is a nationwide centralised electronic funds transfer system owned and operated by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation operates NEFT?

options.A: NPCI

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) operates NEFT.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is RTGS?

options.A: Real Time Gross Settlement, an electronic funds transfer system where transactions are settled individually in real time without netting

questions.explanation: RTGS stands for Real Time Gross Settlement. It is an electronic funds transfer system in which transactions are settled individually in real time, without netting against other transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation operates RTGS in India?

options.A: NPCI

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) operates RTGS.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the minimum amount for an RTGS transaction in India?

options.A: 1 lakh

questions.explanation: The minimum amount for an RTGS transaction is ₹2 lakh. There is no RBI-prescribed upper ceiling, although a bank may set its own channel limits.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What does 'real time' mean in RTGS?

options.A: A payment instruction is processed as it is received rather than being held for later batch processing
options.B: The payment is processed at the end of the day
options.C: The payment is processed only on holidays
options.D: The payment is processed after a week

questions.explanation: Real time means that a payment instruction is processed as it is received rather than being held for later batch processing.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What does 'gross settlement' mean in RTGS?

options.A: Each funds transfer instruction is settled individually without offsetting it against other transactions
options.B: All transactions are netted and settled together
options.C: Only the net amount is settled

questions.explanation: Gross settlement means that each funds transfer instruction is settled individually, without offsetting it against other transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between NEFT and RTGS?

options.A: NEFT processes transactions in settlement batches and supports a wide range of amounts; RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time and has a minimum of ₹2 lakh
options.B: NEFT is only for high-value transfers; RTGS is only for low-value transfers
options.C: NEFT is operated by NPCI; RTGS is operated by SEBI

questions.explanation: NEFT is a nationwide funds transfer system that processes transactions in settlement batches and supports a wide range of amounts. RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time and is designed primarily for high-value transfers, with a minimum transaction amount of ₹2 lakh.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between IMPS and UPI?

options.A: Both support instant interbank payments, but UPI uses a unified interface and payment address/QR-based ecosystem, while IMPS is a separate instant transfer service accessible through supported bank channels
options.B: IMPS is operated by RBI; UPI is operated by SEBI
options.C: UPI is only for high-value transfers; IMPS is only for low-value transfers
options.D: IMPS is not available round the clock

questions.explanation: Both support instant interbank payments and are available round the clock. UPI uses a unified interface and payment address/QR-based ecosystem, while IMPS is a separate instant transfer service accessible through supported bank channels and identifiers.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between UPI and NEFT?

options.A: UPI is designed for instant retail payments through interoperable mobile interfaces, while NEFT is a nationwide bank funds transfer system operated by RBI and processed through settlement batches
options.B: UPI is operated by RBI; NEFT is operated by NPCI
options.C: NEFT is only for retail payments; UPI is only for high-value transfers

questions.explanation: UPI is designed for instant retail payments through interoperable mobile interfaces, while NEFT is a nationwide bank funds transfer system operated by RBI and processed through settlement batches.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between UPI and RTGS?

options.A: UPI is commonly used for retail person-to-person and merchant payments; RTGS is an RBI-operated real-time gross settlement system mainly used for high-value transfers of ₹2 lakh and above
options.B: UPI is operated by RBI; RTGS is operated by NPCI
options.C: RTGS is used for retail payments; UPI is used for high-value transfers
options.D: Both have a minimum transaction limit of ₹2 lakh

questions.explanation: UPI is commonly used for retail person-to-person and merchant payments. RTGS is an RBI-operated real-time gross settlement system mainly used for high-value transfers of ₹2 lakh and above.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is AePS?

options.A: Aadhaar Enabled Payment System, which enables customers to perform supported basic banking transactions through Aadhaar authentication

questions.explanation: AePS stands for Aadhaar Enabled Payment System. It enables customers to perform supported basic banking transactions through Aadhaar authentication at authorised micro-ATMs or business correspondent points.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation operates AePS?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: NPCI operates the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What services can be accessed through AePS?

options.A: Cash withdrawal, cash deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement, Aadhaar fund transfer and other interoperable banking services

questions.explanation: Depending on bank and service availability, AePS can support cash withdrawal, cash deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement, Aadhaar fund transfer or other interoperable banking services.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is APBS?

options.A: Aadhaar Payment Bridge System, an NPCI-operated payment system used to route eligible Aadhaar-based government benefit payments

questions.explanation: APBS stands for Aadhaar Payment Bridge System. It is an NPCI-operated payment system used to route eligible Aadhaar-based government benefit payments to the bank account mapped to the beneficiary's Aadhaar number.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between AePS and APBS?

options.A: AePS enables customers to access basic banking services using Aadhaar authentication at supported service points; APBS is a payment-routing system used mainly for Aadhaar-based Direct Benefit Transfer credits
options.B: AePS is used for DBT; APBS is used for cash withdrawal

questions.explanation: AePS enables customers to access basic banking services using Aadhaar authentication at supported service points. APBS is a payment-routing system used mainly for Aadhaar-based Direct Benefit Transfer credits.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is NACH?

options.A: National Automated Clearing House, an NPCI-operated system for processing high-volume, repetitive and bulk electronic credit and debit transactions

questions.explanation: NACH stands for National Automated Clearing House. It is an NPCI-operated system for processing high-volume, repetitive and bulk electronic credit and debit transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is RuPay?

options.A: An Indian domestic card payment network developed by NPCI supporting debit, credit and prepaid card transactions

questions.explanation: RuPay is an Indian domestic card payment network developed by NPCI. It supports debit, credit and prepaid card transactions through participating institutions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is BBPS?

options.A: Bharat Bill Payment System, an interoperable bill payment ecosystem

questions.explanation: BBPS stands for Bharat Bill Payment System. It is an interoperable bill payment ecosystem that enables customers to pay participating utility and other bills through multiple channels.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is FASTag?

options.A: An electronic toll collection system using RFID technology to enable toll payments without stopping for cash

questions.explanation: FASTag is an electronic toll collection system that uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology to enable toll payments without stopping for cash transactions at supported toll plazas.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a prepaid payment instrument (PPI)?

options.A: A payment instrument in which value is stored in advance and can be used to purchase goods or services or make permitted transfers, subject to RBI regulations

questions.explanation: A PPI is a payment instrument in which value is stored in advance and can be used to purchase goods or services or make permitted transfers, subject to RBI regulations.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a mobile wallet?

options.A: A digital application or service that stores payment credentials or prepaid value and enables electronic transactions
options.B: A physical wallet for carrying cash

questions.explanation: A mobile wallet is a digital application or service that stores payment credentials or prepaid value and enables electronic transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a payment gateway?

options.A: A technology service that securely captures and transmits payment information between a merchant, customer and relevant payment participants
options.B: A physical gate at a bank

questions.explanation: A payment gateway is a technology service that securely captures and transmits payment information between a merchant, customer and relevant payment participants to facilitate an electronic transaction.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a point-of-sale (POS) terminal?

options.A: An electronic device used by merchants to accept payments, commonly through debit cards, credit cards or supported contactless methods

questions.explanation: A POS terminal is an electronic device used by merchants to accept payments, commonly through debit cards, credit cards or supported contactless methods.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a micro-ATM?

options.A: A small handheld banking device used by a business correspondent to provide supported banking services, including Aadhaar-enabled transactions
options.B: A large ATM machine in a bank

questions.explanation: A micro-ATM is a small handheld banking device used by a business correspondent to provide supported banking services, including Aadhaar-enabled transactions where available.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is IFSC?

options.A: Indian Financial System Code, an alphanumeric code used to identify a bank branch for electronic funds transfer systems

questions.explanation: IFSC stands for Indian Financial System Code. It is an alphanumeric code used to identify a bank branch for electronic funds transfer systems such as NEFT, RTGS and IMPS.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is two-factor authentication in digital payments?

options.A: Using two distinct authentication factors to verify a user or authorise a transaction, such as a PIN together with a registered device

questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication uses two distinct authentication factors to verify a user or authorise a transaction, such as a PIN together with a registered device or another approved factor.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What are the advantages of digital payments?

options.A: Speed, convenience, reduced cash handling, transaction records, easier reconciliation, wider payment access and improved transparency

questions.explanation: Advantages include speed, convenience, reduced cash handling, transaction records, easier reconciliation, wider payment access and improved transparency.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What are the risks of digital payments?

options.A: Phishing, fake QR codes, unauthorised access, social engineering, malware, mistaken transfers, SIM-swap fraud and disclosure of confidential credentials

questions.explanation: Risks include phishing, fake QR codes, unauthorised access, social engineering, malware, mistaken transfers, SIM-swap fraud and disclosure of confidential credentials.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Should a person share a UPI PIN to receive money?

options.A: No, a UPI PIN is used to authorise a debit or payment and should not be shared to receive money
options.B: Yes, it is required to receive money
options.C: Yes, but only with family members
options.D: Yes, but only with bank officials

questions.explanation: No. A UPI PIN is used to authorise a debit or payment; it should not be shared to receive money.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a collect request in UPI?

options.A: A request that asks a user to approve a payment from their bank account; users should verify the request and beneficiary before entering a UPI PIN
options.B: A request to open a bank account
options.C: A request to block a UPI ID
options.D: A request to change the UPI PIN

questions.explanation: A collect request asks a user to approve a payment from their bank account. Users should verify the request and the beneficiary before entering a UPI PIN.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a transaction dispute?

options.A: A formal complaint about a payment, such as an unauthorised, failed, duplicate or incorrect transaction, raised through the bank or relevant payment service provider
options.B: A request to open a new account
options.C: A request to increase transaction limits

questions.explanation: A transaction dispute is a formal complaint about a payment, such as an unauthorised, failed, duplicate or incorrect transaction, raised through the bank or relevant payment service provider under applicable procedures.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What should a citizen do after an unauthorised digital payment?

options.A: Immediately contact the bank/payment provider through official channels, report the incident to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 where applicable, and submit a complaint through the official cybercrime reporting portal
options.B: Wait for a week before reporting
options.C: Share the UPI PIN with the bank

questions.explanation: The citizen should immediately contact the bank/payment provider through official channels, report the incident to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 where applicable, and submit a complaint through the official cybercrime reporting portal.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the national cybercrime reporting portal of India?

options.A: cybercrime.gov.in

questions.explanation: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal is the Government of India's online portal at cybercrime.gov.in for reporting specified cybercrime complaints.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is DigiSaathi?

options.A: A 24x7 digital payment information helpline initiative that assists users with queries relating to digital payment products and channels

questions.explanation: DigiSaathi is a 24x7 digital payment information helpline initiative that assists users with queries relating to digital payment products and channels.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is financial inclusion?

options.A: Ensuring that individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services, including payments, savings, credit, insurance and pensions
options.C: Providing loans only to wealthy individuals
options.D: Opening bank branches only in cities

questions.explanation: Financial inclusion means ensuring that individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services, including payments, savings, credit, insurance and pensions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is an online application?

options.A: A request submitted electronically through a government portal, website, mobile application or authorised service centre for a government service, approval, certificate, licence or benefit
options.C: A verbal request to a government officer
options.D: A request submitted through postal mail

questions.explanation: An online application is a request submitted electronically through a government portal, website, mobile application or authorised service centre for a government service, approval, certificate, licence or benefit.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What are the usual stages of an online government application?

options.A: Registration or login, selection of service, form filling, document upload, fee payment, submission, acknowledgement, verification, decision, issue of service output and status tracking

questions.explanation: The usual stages are registration or login, selection of service, form filling, document upload, fee payment if applicable, submission, acknowledgement, verification, decision, issue of service output and status tracking.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is online registration?

options.A: The process of creating a user account or registering an applicant's details electronically to access a service
options.B: Registering a vehicle at the RTO
options.C: Registering a property at the sub-registrar's office
options.D: Registering a complaint at a police station

questions.explanation: Online registration is the process of creating a user account or registering an applicant's details electronically to access a service.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is e-KYC?

options.A: Electronic Know Your Customer, an electronic process used to verify identity and prescribed customer information through authorised digital methods

questions.explanation: e-KYC means electronic Know Your Customer. It is an electronic process used to verify identity and prescribed customer information through authorised digital methods.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is document upload?

options.A: The electronic submission of supporting files such as identity proof, address proof, photographs, marks cards or land records through a portal
options.B: Physically submitting documents at a government office

questions.explanation: Document upload is the electronic submission of supporting files, such as identity proof, address proof, photographs, marks cards or land records, through a portal.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is application verification?

options.A: The process of checking the applicant's identity, submitted documents, eligibility and supporting records before a government decision is made
options.B: The process of submitting an application
options.D: The process of creating a user account

questions.explanation: Application verification is the process of checking the applicant's identity, submitted documents, eligibility and supporting records before a government decision is made.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is an application workflow?

options.A: The defined sequence of steps, officers, checks and approvals through which an application moves from submission to final disposal

questions.explanation: An application workflow is the defined sequence of steps, officers, checks and approvals through which an application moves from submission to final disposal.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is online application tracking?

options.A: A facility that enables applicants to check the status and processing stage of a submitted request using an acknowledgement number or login credentials

questions.explanation: Online application tracking enables applicants to check the status and processing stage of a submitted request using an acknowledgement number or login credentials.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is an online service fee?

options.A: An authorised charge collected electronically for processing or delivering a specified government service
options.C: A fee for opening a bank account
options.D: A charge for using the internet

questions.explanation: An online service fee is an authorised charge collected electronically for processing or delivering a specified government service.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is an electronic acknowledgement?

options.A: A digitally generated confirmation that an application or transaction has been received by the system

questions.explanation: An electronic acknowledgement is a digitally generated confirmation that an application or transaction has been received by the system.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a service delivery timeline?

options.A: The prescribed or published period within which a department is expected or legally required to process and deliver a notified service
options.B: The time taken to submit an application
options.C: The time taken to create a user account
options.D: The time taken to pay fees

questions.explanation: A service delivery timeline is the prescribed or published period within which a department is expected or legally required to process and deliver a notified service.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a single sign-on facility?

options.A: A facility that allows a user to access multiple integrated services using one authentication session or set of credentials
options.B: A facility to sign documents digitally
options.C: A facility to open multiple bank accounts
options.D: A facility to submit multiple applications

questions.explanation: Single sign-on allows a user to access multiple integrated services using one authentication session or set of credentials, subject to the system's security design.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the role of Seva Sindhu in Karnataka?

options.A: It is a Government of Karnataka citizen-service delivery initiative that provides an integrated digital access channel for multiple departmental services
options.B: It is a digital payment system
options.C: It is a land record system
options.D: It is a grievance redressal system

questions.explanation: Seva Sindhu is a Government of Karnataka citizen-service delivery initiative that provides an integrated digital access channel for multiple departmental services.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is Namma Seve or Seva One in Karnataka?

options.A: A Karnataka government citizen-services platform that allows users to search for services, access departments and check application status

questions.explanation: Namma Seve (Seva One) is a Karnataka government citizen-services platform that allows users to search for services, access departments and check application status.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the role of Common Service Centres (CSCs) in online applications?

options.A: They provide assisted access to online government and other services, particularly for citizens who do not have devices, internet access or digital skills

questions.explanation: CSCs provide assisted access to online government and other services, particularly for citizens who do not have devices, internet access or digital skills.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is a Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE)?

options.A: An individual who operates a Common Service Centre and helps citizens access selected digital services and complete online transactions

questions.explanation: A VLE is an individual who operates a Common Service Centre and helps citizens access selected digital services and complete online transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between a government portal and a service centre?

questions.explanation: The Janaspandana helpline number reported by the Karnataka Economic Survey 2024-25 is 1902.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The Bhoomi project was inaugurated in which year?
questions.explanation: The Bhoomi land-records computerisation project was inaugurated in 2000.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The Direct Benefit Transfer programme was launched on which date?

options.A: 1 January 2013

questions.explanation: The Government of India launched the DBT programme on 1 January 2013.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Janaspandana (iPGRS) was launched on which date?

options.A: 1 November 2021

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Economic Survey 2024-25 reports that iPGRS/Janaspandana was launched on 1 November 2021.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The Information Technology Act received presidential assent on which date?

options.A: 9 June 2000

questions.explanation: The Information Technology Act, 2000 received presidential assent on 9 June 2000 and came into force on 17 October 2000.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The minimum amount for an RTGS transaction is:

options.A: ₹1 lakh

questions.explanation: The minimum amount for an RTGS transaction is ₹2 lakh.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The official CPGRAMS website is:

options.A: https://pgportal.gov.in/

questions.explanation: The official CPGRAMS website is https://pgportal.gov.in/.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The official Janaspandana grievance portal is:

options.A: https://ipgrs.karnataka.gov.in/

questions.explanation: The official Janaspandana grievance portal is https://ipgrs.karnataka.gov.in/.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal is at:

options.A: cybercrime.gov.in

questions.explanation: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal is at cybercrime.gov.in.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a risk of digital payments?

options.A: Phishing

questions.explanation: Improved transparency is an advantage, not a risk. Risks include phishing, fake QR codes, unauthorised access, social engineering, malware, mistaken transfers, SIM-swap fraud and disclosure of confidential credentials.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a usual stage of an online government application?

options.A: Registration or login

questions.explanation: The usual stages are registration or login, selection of service, form filling, document upload, fee payment if applicable, submission, acknowledgement, verification, decision, issue of service output and status tracking. Physical verification is not a usual online stage.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common form of digital payment in India?

options.A: UPI

questions.explanation: Cash is a physical payment method, not a digital payment. Common forms include UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, debit and credit cards, AePS, mobile banking, internet banking, PPIs and electronic clearing systems.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a precaution while verifying a digital certificate?

options.A: Check the issuing authority
options.C: Share the private key with the verifier
options.D: Check whether the document has been altered or revoked

questions.explanation: A private key must never be shared. Precautions include checking the issuing authority, document number, digital signature status, validity, QR code or official verification link, and whether the document has been altered or revoked.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a risk or limitation of digital land records?

options.A: Outdated or incorrect entries

questions.explanation: Improved record retrieval is a benefit, not a risk. Risks include outdated or incorrect entries, data mismatch, fraudulent access, cyberattacks, technical outages, incomplete digitisation and disputes requiring legal or field-level verification.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Who operates the Aadhaar Payment Bridge System (APBS)?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: APBS is an NPCI-operated payment system used to route eligible Aadhaar-based government benefit payments.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the role of UIDAI in the context of Aadhaar-based payments?

options.A: UIDAI issues Aadhaar numbers and manages the Aadhaar identity infrastructure

questions.explanation: UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) issues Aadhaar numbers and manages the Aadhaar identity infrastructure used in Aadhaar-based payments and DBT.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is a flagship Digital India initiative associated with digital document storage?

options.A: DigiLocker

questions.explanation: DigiLocker is a Government of India digital document platform under the Digital India programme.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following matters is excluded from CPGRAMS?

options.A: RTI matters

questions.explanation: The CPGRAMS portal identifies excluded categories, including RTI matters, court-related or sub judice matters, religious matters and certain government employee service matters.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stage of online grievance redressal?

options.A: Registration

questions.explanation: The stages generally include registration, acknowledgement, categorisation, assignment to the responsible authority, examination, action or resolution, communication to the complainant, feedback and appeal or escalation where available. Physical hearing in court is not a stage of online grievance redressal.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of DBT?

options.A: Reduced intermediaries

questions.explanation: Increased duplication is a limitation, not a benefit. Benefits include reduced intermediaries, improved traceability, faster payment processing in suitable cases, better beneficiary targeting, reduced duplication and improved financial transparency.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation or risk of DBT?

options.A: Incorrect beneficiary databases

questions.explanation: Improved beneficiary targeting is a benefit, not a limitation. Risks include incorrect beneficiary databases, exclusion due to authentication or account problems, dormant accounts, failed transactions, connectivity barriers, privacy risks and difficulty accessing banking services in remote areas.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a challenge of online applications?

options.A: Poor internet connectivity

questions.explanation: Reduced paperwork is a benefit, not a challenge. Challenges include poor internet connectivity, digital illiteracy, language barriers, inaccessible design, document upload problems, server downtime, data errors and difficulties for people without devices.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of online applications?

options.A: Reduced repeated office visits

questions.explanation: Increased paperwork is a challenge, not a benefit. Benefits include reduced repeated office visits, electronic acknowledgement, status tracking, standardised workflows, reduced paperwork and improved administrative monitoring.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Under which Act is Sakala established?

options.A: The Karnataka Sakala Services Act, 2011
options.C: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007

questions.explanation: Sakala is established under the Karnataka Sakala Services Act, 2011.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a service that can be accessed through AePS?

options.A: Cash withdrawal

questions.explanation: AePS supports cash withdrawal, cash deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement, Aadhaar fund transfer and other interoperable banking services. Property registration is not an AePS service.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What should a citizen do if they receive a UPI collect request from an unknown person?

options.A: Verify the request and beneficiary before entering a UPI PIN
options.C: Share the UPI PIN to verify

questions.explanation: A collect request asks a user to approve a payment from their bank account. Users should verify the request and the beneficiary before entering a UPI PIN.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation operates the National Automated Clearing House (NACH)?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: NACH is an NPCI-operated system for processing high-volume, repetitive and bulk electronic credit and debit transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which organisation developed the RuPay card payment network?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: RuPay is an Indian domestic card payment network developed by NPCI.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Who licenses and regulates Certifying Authorities in India?

options.A: The Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)

questions.explanation: The Controller of Certifying Authorities, under MeitY, licenses and regulates Certifying Authorities and performs statutory functions under the Information Technology Act, 2000.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about DigiLocker issued documents?

options.A: They are made available electronically by a registered issuer
options.B: They can be verified through the DigiLocker ecosystem
options.C: They are automatically authenticated even if uploaded by the user
options.D: They are recognised as legally equivalent to physical originals when used electronically under the applicable IT Act framework

questions.explanation: A user-uploaded document is not automatically verified as an authentic issuer-issued document. Issued documents are made available by a registered issuer and can be verified through the DigiLocker ecosystem.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT contained in an RTC?

options.A: Survey number

questions.explanation: An RTC may contain survey number, land extent, recorded holders or rights, tenancy information, land classification and cultivation/crop details. Encumbrance details are found in an Encumbrance Certificate, not an RTC.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Bhoomi system?

options.A: Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTC)

questions.explanation: Bhoomi is associated with digitisation and online access to RTC and related land-record services, including mutation information. Property registration is handled by Kaveri 2.0.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Janaspandana?

options.A: Multi-channel grievance registration

questions.explanation: Janaspandana provides a multi-channel, paperless and trackable grievance mechanism and monitors time-bound resolution. Issuing digital signatures is not a feature of Janaspandana.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the JAM trinity?

options.A: Jan Dhan

questions.explanation: JAM stands for Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile. PAN is not a component of the JAM trinity.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of RTGS?

options.A: Real-time processing

questions.explanation: RTGS processes transactions in real time and settles each transaction individually (gross settlement). Batch processing is a feature of NEFT, not RTGS.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of NEFT?

options.A: Operated by RBI

questions.explanation: NEFT supports a wide range of amounts and does not have a minimum transaction limit of ₹2 lakh. The ₹2 lakh minimum applies to RTGS.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of digital administration?

options.A: Efficiency

questions.explanation: The main objective of digital administration is to make public administration more efficient, transparent, accountable, accessible, responsive, secure and citizen-centric. Increasing physical paperwork is contrary to this.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a channel for delivering a digital public service?

options.A: Websites

questions.explanation: A digital public service is accessed or completed through electronic channels such as websites, mobile applications, service portals or assisted digital centres. Physical notice boards are not electronic channels.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid precaution to avoid digital payment fraud?

options.A: Never share UPI PIN

questions.explanation: OTPs and UPI PINs should never be shared with anyone, including bank officials. Sharing OTPs is a common cause of digital payment fraud.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: What is the full form of AePS?

options.A: Aadhaar Enabled Payment System

questions.explanation: AePS stands for Aadhaar Enabled Payment System.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid form of digital payment?

options.A: UPI

questions.explanation: A bearer cheque is a paper instrument, not a digital payment. Digital payments include UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, cards, AePS, mobile banking, internet banking, PPIs and electronic clearing systems.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)?

options.A: Licensing Certifying Authorities
options.D: Performing statutory functions under the IT Act, 2000

questions.explanation: The CCA licenses and regulates Certifying Authorities and performs statutory functions under the Information Technology Act, 2000. Issuing UPI PINs is not a function of the CCA.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of digitally signed government certificates?

options.A: Verification of issuing authority
options.D: Electronic verification without depending entirely on physical copies

questions.explanation: Digital signatures reduce forgery risk, not increase it. Benefits include verification of issuing authority, detection of document alteration, reduced forgery risk and electronic verification.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of digital land records?

options.A: Improved record retrieval

questions.explanation: Increased data mismatch is a risk, not a benefit. Benefits include improved record retrieval, transparency, traceability of changes, service access, mutation monitoring, record preservation and coordination among departments.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of an online grievance system?

options.A: Providing an accessible and traceable channel for complaints

questions.explanation: The purpose of an online grievance system is to provide an accessible and traceable channel for complaints, improve accountability, monitor delays, identify recurring service problems and support timely resolution. Increasing pendency is contrary to this.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Janaspandana?

options.A: Multi-channel access

questions.explanation: Janaspandana provides a multi-channel, paperless and trackable grievance mechanism. Physical court hearings are not a characteristic of Janaspandana.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a role of banks in DBT?

options.A: Validating beneficiary account credits

questions.explanation: Eligibility for welfare schemes is determined by the relevant scheme rules and implementing authority, not by banks. Banks validate and process beneficiary account credits, maintain account records, handle payment returns and provide transaction information.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a role of NPCI in Aadhaar-based DBT?

options.A: Operating the Aadhaar Payment Bridge System
options.B: Routing eligible Aadhaar-based transactions between participating banks

questions.explanation: NPCI operates the Aadhaar Payment Bridge System and related payment infrastructure used to route eligible Aadhaar-based transactions between participating banks. Issuing Aadhaar numbers is the role of UIDAI, not NPCI.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason for a DBT payment failure?

options.A: Invalid account details
options.D: Beneficiary has valid Aadhaar and active account

questions.explanation: A DBT payment failure occurs when a transfer cannot be credited to the intended beneficiary due to invalid account details, inactive accounts, mapping issues or other technical or banking reasons. A valid Aadhaar and active account do not cause payment failure.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Karnataka-specific digital administration system?

options.A: Bhoomi

questions.explanation: CPGRAMS is the Government of India's central public grievance portal. Bhoomi, e-Swathu and Kaveri 2.0 are Karnataka-specific systems.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Karnataka-specific citizen service platform?

options.A: Seva Sindhu

questions.explanation: DigiLocker is a Government of India digital document platform. Seva Sindhu, Namma Seve and Seva One are Karnataka government citizen service platforms.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about UPI is correct?

options.A: UPI was developed by RBI
options.B: UPI was launched in 2016 by NPCI
options.C: UPI requires sharing bank account number and IFSC for every transaction
options.D: UPI is a batch processing system

questions.explanation: UPI was developed by NPCI and launched in 2016. It uses a VPA/UPI ID and does not necessarily require sharing bank account number and IFSC. It processes payments in real time, not in batches.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about RTGS is correct?

options.A: RTGS processes transactions in settlement batches
options.C: RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time
options.D: RTGS has no minimum transaction limit

questions.explanation: RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time. It is operated by RBI and has a minimum transaction limit of ₹2 lakh.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about NEFT is correct?

options.A: NEFT processes transactions in settlement batches
options.C: NEFT settles each transaction individually in real time
options.D: NEFT has a minimum transaction limit of ₹2 lakh

questions.explanation: NEFT processes transactions in settlement batches. It is operated by RBI, supports a wide range of amounts, and does not have a minimum transaction limit of ₹2 lakh.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about digital signatures is correct?

options.A: A digital signature is a scanned image of a handwritten signature
options.B: A digital signature uses public-key cryptography to authenticate the signer and verify integrity
options.C: A digital signature can be created without a private key
options.D: A digital signature does not require a Certifying Authority

questions.explanation: A digital signature is a cryptographic mechanism that uses public-key cryptography to authenticate the signer and help verify the integrity of an electronic record. It is not a scanned image.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about DigiLocker is correct?

options.A: DigiLocker is a Karnataka state government initiative
options.B: DigiLocker is a Government of India digital document platform under the Digital India programme
options.C: DigiLocker is a digital payment system
options.D: DigiLocker is a land record system

questions.explanation: DigiLocker is a Government of India digital document platform under the Digital India programme that enables citizens to access, store, retrieve and share authentic electronic documents.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mutation is correct?

options.A: Mutation conclusively establishes ownership title
options.B: Mutation is the process of updating revenue records to reflect changes in recorded rights or interests
options.C: Mutation is the same as property registration
options.D: Mutation is issued by the court

questions.explanation: Mutation is the process of updating revenue records to reflect a change in recorded rights or interests. Mutation by itself does not conclusively establish ownership title.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an Encumbrance Certificate (EC) is correct?

options.A: An EC guarantees that a property has no legal problem
options.B: An EC shows registered transactions or encumbrances relating to a specified property for a specified period
options.C: An EC replaces a title deed
options.D: An EC is issued by the court

questions.explanation: An Encumbrance Certificate is a record/search certificate showing registered transactions or encumbrances relating to a specified property for a specified period. It does not guarantee that a property has no legal problem.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about CPGRAMS is correct?

options.A: CPGRAMS is a Karnataka state grievance portal
options.B: CPGRAMS is the Government of India's central public grievance portal
options.C: CPGRAMS is a digital payment system
options.D: CPGRAMS is a land record system

questions.explanation: CPGRAMS is the Government of India's online platform for citizens to lodge and track public grievances relating to service delivery.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Janaspandana is correct?

options.A: Janaspandana is the Government of India's central grievance portal
options.B: Janaspandana is Karnataka's state-level grievance platform
options.C: Janaspandana is a digital payment system
options.D: Janaspandana is a land record system

questions.explanation: Janaspandana, also known as the Integrated Public Grievance Redressal System (iPGRS), is Karnataka's state-level grievance platform.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Sakala is correct?

options.A: Sakala is a grievance redressal platform
options.B: Sakala is a statutory framework guaranteeing time-bound delivery of notified services
options.C: Sakala is a digital payment system
options.D: Sakala is a land record system

questions.explanation: Sakala is a statutory framework under the Karnataka Sakala Services Act, 2011, guaranteeing time-bound delivery of notified services and providing appeal/accountability mechanisms.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about DBT is correct?

options.A: DBT determines eligibility for welfare schemes
options.B: DBT is a mechanism for transferring government benefits directly to eligible beneficiaries
options.C: DBT guarantees that every eligible person receives the benefit without failure
options.D: DBT is a retail digital payment system

questions.explanation: DBT is a mechanism through which government benefits are transferred directly to eligible beneficiaries. Eligibility is determined by scheme rules, and successful delivery depends on accurate records and valid payment details.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the RTGS minimum amount is correct?

options.A: The RBI-prescribed minimum is ₹2 lakh, but banks may set their own channel limits
options.C: There is no minimum amount for RTGS

questions.explanation: The 2 lakh RTGS minimum is the RBI-prescribed floor; bank channels may apply their own operational limits.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about APBS is correct?

options.A: APBS is used for Aadhaar authentication at micro-ATMs
options.B: APBS is a payment-routing system used mainly for Aadhaar-based Direct Benefit Transfer credits
options.D: APBS is a type of mobile wallet

questions.explanation: APBS is an NPCI-operated payment-routing system used mainly for Aadhaar-based Direct Benefit Transfer credits. AePS is used for Aadhaar authentication at micro-ATMs.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about AePS is correct?

options.A: AePS is used for routing DBT credits
options.B: AePS enables customers to perform basic banking transactions through Aadhaar authentication at authorised points
options.D: AePS is a type of mobile wallet

questions.explanation: AePS (Aadhaar Enabled Payment System) enables customers to perform supported basic banking transactions through Aadhaar authentication at authorised micro-ATMs or business correspondent points. It is operated by NPCI.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a document URI in DigiLocker is correct?

options.A: It is a type of digital signature
options.B: It is a unique identifier or reference used to locate and retrieve an electronic document from the issuer's repository
options.D: It is a digital payment method

questions.explanation: A document URI is a unique identifier or reference used to locate and retrieve an electronic document from the issuer's repository through the DigiLocker ecosystem.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Tippan is correct?

options.A: Tippan is a type of land tax
options.B: Tippan is a survey-related field sketch or measurement record used in land-survey and boundary-related administration in Karnataka
options.D: Tippan is a property registration document

questions.explanation: A Tippan is a survey-related field sketch or measurement record used in land-survey and boundary-related administration in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Form 9 and Form 11 in e-Swathu is correct?

options.A: They are income tax forms
options.B: They are prescribed rural property-related records/forms used in Gram Panchayat property administration

questions.explanation: Form 9 and Form 11 are prescribed rural property-related records/forms used in Gram Panchayat property administration. The exact form and purpose should be understood according to the applicable rules and current system.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about grievance analytics is correct?

options.A: It helps government identify recurring problems, departments with high pendency, service bottlenecks and geographic patterns
options.C: It replaces the need for grievance redressal
options.D: It is only for statistical record-keeping

questions.explanation: Grievance analytics helps government identify recurring problems, departments with high pendency, service bottlenecks, geographic patterns and issues requiring policy or process correction.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the relationship between grievance redressal and RTI is correct?

options.A: Grievance redressal seeks action or resolution of a complaint; RTI is a legal mechanism to obtain information held by public authorities
options.C: RTI seeks action on complaints; grievance redressal seeks information
options.D: Grievance redressal is a court procedure

questions.explanation: Grievance redressal seeks action or resolution of a complaint. RTI is a legal mechanism to obtain information held by public authorities; it is not a substitute for a service grievance.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NPCI mapper is correct?

options.A: It maps bank account numbers to IFSC codes
options.B: It maps Aadhaar numbers to the bank enabled to receive Aadhaar-based payments through APBS
options.C: It maps mobile numbers to bank accounts
options.D: It maps PAN numbers to Aadhaar

questions.explanation: The NPCI mapper is a system used to map Aadhaar numbers to the bank that is enabled to receive Aadhaar-based payments through the Aadhaar Payment Bridge System.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about account-based DBT vs Aadhaar-based DBT is correct?

options.A: Account-based DBT uses Aadhaar mapping; Aadhaar-based DBT uses account numbers
options.B: Account-based DBT uses beneficiary bank account details such as account number and IFSC; Aadhaar-based DBT uses Aadhaar mapping through APBS

questions.explanation: Account-based DBT uses beneficiary bank account details such as account number and IFSC to route payment. Aadhaar-based DBT uses Aadhaar mapping through APBS to identify the destination bank account.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bapuji Seva Kendras is correct?

options.A: They provide assisted access to citizen services at Gram Panchayat level

questions.explanation: Bapuji Seva Kendras are associated with delivery of selected citizen services at Gram Panchayat level.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bangalore One and Karnataka One is correct?

options.A: They provide assisted citizen access in rural areas
options.B: They provide selected government and utility services through integrated service centres and digital channels in urban areas

questions.explanation: Bangalore One and Karnataka One provide selected government and utility services through integrated service centres and digital channels, primarily in urban areas.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Why is integration between Bhoomi, e-Swathu and Kaveri 2.0 important?

options.A: It increases data entry work
options.B: It improves consistency and retrieval of relevant property information during registration and land/property administration, reducing repeated data entry and discrepancies
options.D: It eliminates the need for surveys

questions.explanation: Integration can improve consistency and retrieval of relevant property information during registration and land/property administration, while reducing repeated data entry and discrepancies.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 is correct?

options.A: It provides the legal framework for regulation and supervision of payment systems in India by the RBI
options.C: It is related only to agricultural payments
options.D: It is related only to international payments

questions.explanation: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 provides the legal framework for regulation and supervision of payment systems in India by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about two-factor authentication is correct?

options.A: It uses two distinct authentication factors to verify a user or authorise a transaction
options.B: It uses two different bank accounts
options.C: It uses two different mobile phones

questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication uses two distinct authentication factors to verify a user or authorise a transaction, such as a PIN together with a registered device or another approved factor.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about FASTag is correct?

options.A: It uses RFID technology for electronic toll collection
options.B: It is a type of bank account
options.C: It is a government identity card

questions.explanation: FASTag is an electronic toll collection system that uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology to enable toll payments without stopping for cash transactions.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about BBPS is correct?

options.A: It is an interoperable bill payment ecosystem
options.B: It is a type of mobile wallet
options.C: It is a government identity card
options.D: It is a land record system

questions.explanation: BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System) is an interoperable bill payment ecosystem that enables customers to pay participating utility and other bills through multiple channels.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a prepaid payment instrument (PPI) is correct?

options.A: Value is stored in advance and can be used to purchase goods or services or make permitted transfers, subject to RBI regulations
options.B: It is a post-paid credit card
options.C: It is a type of bank loan

questions.explanation: A PPI is a payment instrument in which value is stored in advance and can be used to purchase goods or services or make permitted transfers, subject to RBI regulations.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a payment gateway is correct?

options.A: It securely captures and transmits payment information between a merchant, customer and relevant payment participants
options.B: It is a physical gate at a bank
options.C: It is a government portal for taxes
options.D: It is a type of bank account

questions.explanation: A payment gateway is a technology service that securely captures and transmits payment information between a merchant, customer and relevant payment participants to facilitate an electronic transaction.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a micro-ATM is correct?

options.A: It is a small handheld banking device used by a business correspondent to provide supported banking services
options.B: It is a large ATM machine in a bank
options.C: It is a type of mobile phone

questions.explanation: A micro-ATM is a small handheld banking device used by a business correspondent to provide supported banking services, including Aadhaar-enabled transactions where available.

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following statements about DigiSaathi is correct?

options.A: It is a 24x7 digital payment information helpline initiative
options.B: It is a government scheme for farmers
options.C: It is a type of digital wallet

questions.subject: Digital Administration

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is a small handheld banking device used by a business correspondent to provide supported banking services?

options.A: Micro-ATM

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is a technology service that securely captures and transmits payment information between a merchant, customer and relevant payment participants?

options.A: Payment gateway

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is a request that asks a user to approve a payment from their bank account through UPI?

options.A: Collect request

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is a formal complaint about a payment, such as an unauthorised, failed, duplicate or incorrect transaction?

questions.subject: Digital Administration

questions.subject: Digital Administration

questions.subject: Digital Administration

options.A: Electronic certificate

questions.subject: Digital Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is an electronic document authenticated using a digital signature so that the recipient can verify its issuer and detect unauthorised changes?

questions.subject: Digital Administration

questions.subject: Digital Administration
